_meta.name: rosch1975_typicality
_meta.purpose: Human category-typicality baseline for the gated-minting capability suite. Each category lists members with a human typicality RANK (1 = best/most typical example) and a normalized typicality SCORE in [0,1] (1.0 = most typical). This is the ground truth against which the substrate's minted fine-grained axis (and, optionally, LLM embeddings) are scored for Rubric A RQ2 (Spearman rho of system item-order vs human typicality-order).
_meta.source_of_truth: Eleanor Rosch (1975), 'Cognitive representations of semantic categories', Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 104(3):192-233 — the canonical goodness-of-example / typicality norms. The compression-vs-meaning paper we anchor on (Soffer, Jurafsky, LeCun, Shwartz-Ziv, 'From Tokens to Thoughts', arXiv:2505.17117) digitizes exactly these Rosch (1975) norms (plus Rosch 1973 and McCloskey & Glucksberg 1978) as its released human benchmark.
_meta.provenance_honesty: This file is a FAITHFUL RECONSTRUCTION of the well-established Rosch (1975) rank orderings, NOT a byte-copy of either Rosch's original rating table or the arXiv:2505.17117 supplement (the paper's CSV supplement was not publicly fetchable at build time, and the primary-source PDFs blocked direct download). The RANK ORDER within each category reproduces the canonical, repeatedly-replicated human ordering (e.g. robin/sparrow most typical birds; penguin/ostrich/bat least; chair/sofa most typical furniture; orange/apple most typical fruit). The SCORE column is a monotonic normalization of the rank (score = 1 - (rank-1)/(n-1)), a stand-in for the exact 1-7 mean rating — it PRESERVES THE ORDER (which is what the Spearman-rho metric consumes) but is NOT the exact mean rating value. When the exact Rosch/arXiv values become available, replace the scores; the ranks should already match. Any capability claim scored off this file must cite it as a reconstruction, not as Rosch's raw data.
_meta.metric_consumed_by: Rubric A RQ2 — Spearman rank correlation (rho) between a system's induced item ordering (e.g. item-to-set-point distance) and the human typicality RANK here. Published reference points from arXiv:2505.17117: most decoder LLMs rho < 0.2; BERT rho ~ 0.38; humans define the ground truth (rho = 1.0 by construction).
_meta.license: The underlying norms are published scientific facts (Rosch 1975). This reconstruction is released under the repository's license for research use. Attribution: Rosch (1975), JEP:General 104(3):192-233.
